summary: Anything in the notification feed can now be put straight into a case file, from the screen where you noticed it. Until now the only route was to read the time off the row, go to the timeline, find the moment again and bookmark it — which loses any record of what you were looking at and takes long enough that it mostly did not happen. Every row now has an Add to case button, and the recorder works out for itself what the entry actually refers to: an entry about an AI detection goes in as that detection, with its own camera, time and picture, so the same piece of evidence can never end up in a case twice under two different names. An entry about a camera keeps the footage either side of the moment, and the case holds it against retention like any other evidence. And an entry about the machine itself — a restart, a disk filling — goes in too, with no footage, because that is often the fact that explains the gap in the recording either side of it. Your note goes in with it either way.
compatibility: Purely additive: existing cases and their exports are untouched, and nothing changes for anybody who does not press the new button. Two things worth knowing. An entry with no camera holds no footage — it is a fact with a time on it, not a clip, and the case says so rather than implying there is video to export. And where an entry refers to a detection that retention has since deleted, the entry itself still goes into the case: you keep the record of what was seen and when, which is the part a case needs, instead of a button that quietly stops working on older rows. Also fixed while adding this: the Add button in the case dialog could not be pressed at all when there was no timeline selection behind it.
